label: Bodily nature as cognitive object…: A nature n occurring in CanUnderstand intellect n is an object…
term: bodily nature as cognitive object rather than constitution
definition: A nature n occurring in CanUnderstand intellect n is an object of the represented capacity, not thereby a constitutive bodily nature of the intellectual principle. This interface distinction does not assert a modern material theory of representation, nor does it supply an account of intentionality.
note: Needed to prevent a content/constitution equivocation. The source q.75 a.1 ad 2 distinguishes a likeness received potentially from what is naturally actual in a knower; that context motivates keeping the relations separate without formalizing the complete reception account.

formal_gap.meaning: Question75.Article2.Model.CanUnderstand i n says that the intellectual principle i can understand the nature n: n is an object of its cognitive capacity. It is a supplied relation in the q.75 a.2 model.
examples: A human intellect able to understand the nature of fire, among the natures of all bodies (q.75 a.2).
exclusions: Having n naturally as one's own constitution (HasNaturally): a known bodily nature is not thereby a constitutive nature of the knower (DISAMB-Q75-NATURAL-AND-REPRESENTED-NATURE).
A modern material theory of representation or an account of intentionality.
open_obligations: The complete reception account of q.75 a.1 ad 2 (a likeness received potentially) is not formalized.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
